intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

selected_hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Explore the medieval heart of Prague on foot. Watch the famous Orloj clock strike the hour, wander through Staroměstské náměstí (Old Town Square), and discover Gothic churches and Baroque palaces. Stay near Old Town to maximize walking access and avoid transit time after a late arrival — by Day 2 morning you are already steps away from the action.

experiences.name: Czech Street Food & Local Market Crawl
experiences.description: Sample trdelník, svíčková, and craft Czech beer at Manifesto Market and Náplavka Farmers Market along the Vltava riverbank. This riverside hub is walkable from centrally located hotels in New Town or Old Town, making it ideal even on arrival day if you land by early afternoon — coordinators recommend rebooking flights to arrive by 14:00 to enjoy this on Day 1 evening.
experiences.location: Náplavka Riverbank, New Town (Nové Město), Prague

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl in the Jewish Quarter
experiences.description: Experience Budapest's iconic ruin bar scene starting at Szimpla Kert, the original ruin pub, surrounded by eclectic décor and local craft drinks. The Jewish Quarter is a compact, walkable neighborhood — staying in District VII puts you within 5 minutes of all major ruin bars, addressing coordinator concerns about hotel proximity to activity hubs.

experiences.name: Buda Castle Hill & Hungarian History Walk
experiences.description: Climb or take the funicular up to Buda Castle, visit the Hungarian National Gallery, Matthias Church, and Fisherman's Bastion for panoramic views over the Danube and Pest. Book a guided walking tour departing from Castle Hill directly — staying in District I or near the Chain Bridge eliminates long commutes flagged by the coordinator.

experiences.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath Experience
experiences.description: Unwind in one of Europe's largest thermal bath complexes, a Budapest institution since 1913. Soak in mineral-rich outdoor and indoor pools surrounded by stunning Neo-Baroque architecture. Located in City Park, it is easily accessible from centrally booked hotels in Districts VI or VII — a 10-minute walk or short metro ride, resolving the proximity issues noted by the coordinator.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Land at 13:00, clear customs, and take the Airport Express Bus (Line AE) to Náměstí Republiky for ~60 CZK (~€2.50), then walk or take the metro to your hotel in Staré Město. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed self-guided walk through Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí) to get your bearings — admire the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the Gothic Church of Our Lady before Týn. No rush, just soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge at sunset for free — a magical first Prague experience. Watch the golden light hit the castle and statues. Then explore the narrow cobblestone lanes of Malá Strana just across the bridge.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and cheap 'chlebíčky' (open-faced sandwich) or trdelník pastry from a street stall near Old Town Square for under 60 CZK (~€2.50).
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33) — a beloved local Czech pub with affordable traditional dishes like svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings for around 200–280 CZK (~€8–11). Pair with a cheap Pilsner Urquell draft.

day_by_day.notes: Get a 24-hour public transport pass (120 CZK / ~€5) upon arrival — it covers bus, metro, and tram and is excellent value. Download the 'PID Lítačka' app for easy ticket purchases. Exchange some cash to CZK as many local spots prefer it.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle in the world. Take Tram 22 from Malostranské náměstí up the hill. Walk through the castle grounds (outer areas are FREE), visit St. Vitus Cathedral (free to enter the nave), and enjoy panoramic views over the red rooftops of Prague. Budget option: skip the paid interior tours and focus on the free exterior areas and viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood. Visit the Baroque St. Nicholas Church (entry ~100 CZK / ~€4) and browse the quiet side streets. Head to Petřín Hill — take the funicular (covered by public transport pass) for sweeping city views. The Petřín Lookout Tower is a mini Eiffel Tower replica with great panoramas (entry ~150 CZK / ~€6).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Old Town and explore the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) from the outside — the streets are free to walk. Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery area at dusk for a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere. Then enjoy a casual evening beer at a local pivnice (pub).

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy or grab fresh pastries and coffee from a local bakery near Old Town for under 100 CZK (~€4). Try a 'rohlík' roll with butter and ham.
meals.lunch: Nase Maso (Dlouhá 39) — a beloved local butcher-deli with incredible Czech meat sandwiches and burgers for 150–200 CZK (~€6–8). Very popular with locals.
meals.dinner: U Fleků — one of Prague's oldest breweries (est. 1499) in Nové Město. Try the dark lager brewed on-site with a hearty pork knuckle or schnitzel. Expect to spend around 300–400 CZK (~€12–16) including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: September in Prague is beautiful — mild temperatures around 15–20°C with occasional rain. Pack a light jacket and a small umbrella. The castle is best visited on a weekday morning to avoid tour group crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — two authentic, less-touristy districts loved by locals. Walk up to the Žižkov Television Tower (entry ~250 CZK / ~€10 for the observation deck) for the best 360° view of Prague. The tower also features quirky giant baby sculptures by David Černý crawling up its sides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum (Národní muzeum) on Wenceslas Square — recently renovated and excellent for Czech history and natural history (entry ~250 CZK / ~€10, or free on first Monday of the month). Walk the length of Wenceslas Square (Václavské náměstí), the heart of modern Prague and site of the 1989 Velvet Revolution. Visit the Memorial to the Victims of Communism nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening to explore Prague's vibrant nightlife or catch a classical music concert — Prague is famous for affordable classical performances in historic churches. Check 'Prague Classical Concerts' for tickets starting from ~400 CZK (~€16). Alternatively, join a cheap Prague Legends walking tour.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a local 'kavárna' (café) in Vinohrady — try Café Jedna or a neighborhood bakery for coffee and pastries under 120 CZK (~€5).
meals.lunch: Kantýna (Politických vězňů 5) — a stylish but affordable Czech canteen with daily specials (polévka soup + main) for around 200–250 CZK (~€8–10). Very popular with office workers.
meals.dinner: Pivnice U Pivrnce — a classic Prague pub in Nové Město with cheap Czech staples like fried cheese (smažený sýr), goulash, and local beers. Budget around 200–280 CZK (~€8–11) for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: This is a great day to buy a souvenir or two — avoid the tourist trap shops on Charles Bridge and instead browse Vinohrady's local shops for better prices and quality Czech goods like Bohemian crystal or marionette puppets.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip option OR explore more of Prague. Recommended: Visit Vyšehrad Fortress — a free hilltop fortress with a cemetery where famous Czechs like Dvořák and Smetana are buried. Stunning views of the Vltava River and far fewer tourists than Prague Castle. Walk along the riverbank back toward the center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mucha Museum (Muchovo muzeum) dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alphonse Mucha — entry ~280 CZK (~€11). Explore the stunning Art Nouveau Municipal House (Obecní dům) nearby — the interior is free to peek at in the lobby. Walk through the Powder Tower (Prašná brána) area.
day_by_day.evening: Last evening in Prague — pack your bags for tomorrow's travel to Budapest. Enjoy a farewell Czech dinner and a final walk across Charles Bridge at night when it's atmospheric and less crowded.

meals.breakfast: Eska Bakery (Pernerova 49, Karlín district) — one of Prague's best sourdough bakeries. Worth the short tram ride for fresh bread, pastries, and coffee under 150 CZK (~€6).
meals.lunch: Street food at Manifesto Market (seasonal food truck park) — diverse options from tacos to burgers to Asian food, most dishes 150–200 CZK (~€6–8).
meals.dinner: Restaurace Mlejnice — a hidden gem near Old Town with authentic Czech food at very fair prices. Try the roast duck with red cabbage and dumplings for ~280 CZK (~€11). Great atmosphere with wooden interiors.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Budapest transport tonight if not already done. The best budget option is the RegioJet overnight bus or train from Prague to Budapest — book at regiojet.com. Buses are cheapest (~€15–25) and depart from Florenc Bus Station. Journey is approximately 7–8 hours. A daytime train is also scenic and comfortable.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart Prague early morning by bus or train to Budapest. If taking RegioJet bus (~7–8 hrs), enjoy the scenic Central European countryside. Arrive in Budapest by early-to-mid afternoon. Check into your Budapest accommodation (budget hostels like Maverick City Lodge or Wombats Budapest in the 7th District are great value at €15–25/night). The 7th District (Jewish Quarter) is the ideal base.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive and settle in. Take a gentle orientation walk through the vibrant 7th District (Erzsébetváros) — Budapest's Jewish Quarter and ruin bar capital. Visit the stunning Great Synagogue (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe. Entry ~5,000 HUF (~€13). Walk Kazinczy utca and Király utca streets to feel the neighborhood's unique energy.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's famous ruin bar scene — visit Szimpla Kert (Kazinczy u. 14), the original and most iconic ruin bar. It's free to enter, with cheap local beers (~600–800 HUF / ~€1.50–2). Eclectic decor, live music, and a true Budapest institution. Perfect low-cost evening.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the bus/train or grab something at Prague's Florenc Bus Station before departure.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic lunch from a Czech supermarket (Albert or Billa) before departure — bread, cheese, cold cuts — for under 150 CZK (~€6).
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food (outside Szimpla Kert) — a cluster of food trucks serving langos (Hungarian fried dough with sour cream and cheese, ~1,500 HUF / ~€4), burgers, and more. Perfect budget street dinner in the heart of the Jewish Quarter.

day_by_day.notes: Budapest uses Hungarian Forints (HUF). As of 2027, budget roughly 400–420 HUF per €1. Withdraw cash from ATMs (avoid airport exchange counters). Get a 24-hour Budapest transit pass (~2,500 HUF / ~€6) — it covers all metro, trams, and buses.

day_by_day.morning: Buda Castle Hill (Budavári Palota) — take the historic funicular (Budavári Sikló) from Clark Ádám tér (~1,400 HUF / ~€3.50 one way) or walk up for free. Explore the Castle District on foot: visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom, entry ~2,500 HUF / ~€6) and the Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — one of the most photogenic spots in all of Europe with panoramic views over the Danube and Pest. The exterior terraces are free to walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) on foot back to Pest — enjoy spectacular river views. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) from the outside — the exterior along the Danube is breathtaking and free. If budget allows, interior tours are ~8,500 HUF (~€20) but must be booked in advance. Walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) toward the haunting Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — a powerful and free Holocaust memorial.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — Budapest's largest and most colorful indoor market. Closes around 17:00 on Sundays so time accordingly. Browse stalls of paprika, salami, folk crafts, and local produce. Then enjoy a relaxed evening in the Jewish Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Retró Lángos (multiple locations) or grab fresh pastries from a local 'pékség' (bakery) — try a 'kifli' (crescent roll) or 'rétes' (strudel) for under 500 HUF (~€1.20).
meals.lunch: Hungarikum Bisztró (Steindl Imre u. 13, near Parliament) — excellent traditional Hungarian lunch with goulash soup, chicken paprikash, or stuffed peppers for 2,000–3,000 HUF (~€5–7). Very popular with locals.
meals.dinner: Padron (Kertész u. 29) — a beloved neighborhood bistro in the 7th District with seasonal Hungarian-inspired dishes at very reasonable prices. Expect to spend 3,000–4,500 HUF (~€7–11) for a full meal with a glass of wine.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a great day to visit the Great Market Hall as it closes early — plan accordingly. The Fisherman's Bastion is magical in morning light and gets very crowded by midday, so aim to arrive before 10:00.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian National Museum (Magyar Nemzeti Múzeum) — excellent for understanding Hungarian history from the Magyar conquest to the 20th century. Entry ~3,200 HUF (~€7.50). Then walk to the stunning St. Stephen's Basilica (Szent István-bazilika) — free to enter the main nave, small fee (~500 HUF) to see the Holy Right Hand relic. Climb the dome for panoramic views (~1,500 HUF / ~€3.50).
day_by_day.afternoon: Treat yourself to the iconic Budapest thermal bath experience — visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath (Széchenyi gyógyfürdő) in City Park, one of the largest and most famous in Europe. Weekday entry ~8,500–10,000 HUF (~€20–24) depending on cabin/locker option. Soak in the outdoor pools surrounded by stunning Neo-Baroque architecture — a true Budapest bucket-list experience. Spend 2–3 hours relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through City Park (Városliget) — visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) for free, a grand monument to Hungarian history. As dusk falls, head back toward the Danube for the famous Budapest 'Blue Hour' — the city skyline lit up at night is world-class. Consider a cheap cruise on the Danube (~5,000–7,000 HUF / ~€12–17) for the best nighttime views.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud (Vörösmarty tér) — a historic Budapest institution since 1858. Splurge slightly on coffee and a slice of Dobos torte (~2,500 HUF / ~€6). Worth it for the experience and stunning interior.
meals.lunch: Bring snacks to Széchenyi Baths or grab a quick 'lángos' or sandwich from a nearby kiosk in City Park for under 1,500 HUF (~€3.50).
meals.dinner: Menza (Liszt Ferenc tér 2) — a retro-style Hungarian restaurant on the famous Liszt Ferenc Square with excellent value set menus and classic Hungarian dishes. Budget 3,500–5,000 HUF (~€8–12) for two courses and a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit and a small towel (or rent one at Széchenyi for ~500 HUF) for the thermal baths. Book online in advance to save time and sometimes get a slight discount. Monday is less crowded than weekends at the baths.

day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Budapest — visit the Dohány Street Synagogue complex fully if not done on Day 5, including the moving Holocaust memorial garden (Tree of Life sculpture). Then explore the stylish Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's Champs-Élysées — walking toward the Opera House (Magyar Állami Operaház). The exterior is free; guided tours are available for ~3,500 HUF (~€8) if time permits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping at the Great Market Hall (open until 17:00 weekdays) — pick up Hungarian paprika, Pick salami, Unicum liqueur, or hand-embroidered folk items at fair prices. Then head to the airport or train station for your onward journey. Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport is reachable by Bus 100E (~900 HUF / ~€2.20 direct from Deák Ferenc tér) — the most budget-friendly option.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or final evening in Budapest. If departing late, enjoy one last sunset walk along the Danube or a farewell 'fröccs' (Hungarian wine spritzer) at a terrace bar near the river.

meals.breakfast: New York Café (Erzsébet krt. 9-11) — the 'most beautiful café in the world.' Splurge on a coffee and pastry (~3,000 HUF / ~€7) in the jaw-dropping gilded interior as a farewell treat. Alternatively, grab a cheap breakfast from a local bakery.
meals.lunch: Bors GasztroBar (Kazinczy u. 10) — a cult-favorite tiny sandwich and soup bar in the Jewish Quarter. Incredible sourdough sandwiches and rich soups for 1,500–2,500 HUF (~€3.50–6). Usually a short queue but worth it.
meals.dinner: If staying for dinner: Kőleves (Kazinczy u. 37) — a warm, welcoming Jewish Quarter restaurant with Hungarian-Jewish fusion dishes, great vegetarian options, and a lovely courtyard. Budget 3,500–5,000 HUF (~€8–12) for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the journey to the airport and check-in. Bus 100E runs frequently from central Budapest. Overall trip budget summary: Prague (4 nights) ~€150–200 total including accommodation, food, transport, and entry fees; Budapest (3 nights) ~€130–180 total. Grand total for 8 days: approximately €280–380 per person, excluding flights — very achievable on a budget!

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town) via Airport Express bus + metro or taxi (~45–60 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed introductory stroll through Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí). Watch the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime on the hour, admire the Church of Our Lady before Týn, and wander the Gothic lanes nearby. Pick up a city map and get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric streets of Josefov (the Jewish Quarter) at dusk. Enjoy a leisurely dinner at a traditional Czech restaurant in Old Town, then take a short evening walk across Charles Bridge for stunning night views of Prague Castle.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near Old Town Square after check-in — try a local bakery for trdelník or a sandwich from a café like Café Louvre satellite spots in Old Town
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá St.) — beloved Czech gastropub; try svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or roast pork with dumplings; mid-range pricing, excellent Czech beer on tap

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Focus on soaking in the atmosphere rather than ticking off major sights. Book Charles Bridge walk for evening when crowds thin out.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex visit (Pražský hrad) — one of the largest castle complexes in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička), and the castle gardens. Arrive early (~9:00) to beat crowds. Take tram 22 from Old Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) — explore the charming baroque neighborhood. Visit the ornate St. Nicholas Church, browse Nerudova Street's artisan shops, and stroll through Wallenstein Garden (free entry). Cross Charles Bridge back toward Old Town.
day_by_day.evening: Discover Vinohrady neighborhood for dinner — a residential gem beloved by locals. Afterward, enjoy a craft beer at one of Prague's acclaimed craft beer bars in Old Town such as Craft Beer Spot or Pivovarský klub.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try Café Savoy (Malá Strana) for a beautiful Art Nouveau setting with fresh pastries and eggs
meals.lunch: Malá Strana lunch at U Malé Velryby (The Little Whale) — cozy Czech bistro with daily specials and fair prices
meals.dinner: Eska (Holešovice/tram ride) or closer option: Sansho — creative Czech cuisine with local ingredients; mid-range, reservations recommended

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle ticket: Circuit B (~350 CZK / ~€15) covers the key highlights. Wear comfortable shoes — lots of cobblestones and uphill walking. September weather is typically mild and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Old Jewish Quarter (Josefov) properly — tour the Jewish Museum complex including the Old Jewish Cemetery, Pinkas Synagogue (Holocaust memorial), Spanish Synagogue, and Maisel Synagogue. One of the most moving historical sites in Central Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nové Město (New Town) — walk Wenceslas Square, visit the National Museum (reopened after major renovation), and browse the Lucerna Passage for its quirky upside-down horse sculpture. Head to the Mucha Museum for stunning Art Nouveau works.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague has world-class performances in historic venues (Rudolfinum, Municipal House, or Lobkowicz Palace). Book tickets in advance online. Return to Old Town for a nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Mistral Café (Old Town) — popular local spot with excellent coffee, avocado toast, and eggs
meals.lunch: Lunch near Wenceslas Square — try Café Imperial (stunning 1914 tiled interior) for Czech classics like goulash; mid-range splurge
meals.dinner: Pre-concert light dinner: Červená Karkulka (Little Red Riding Hood) wine bar — charcuterie, cheese boards, and Czech wines; relaxed and affordable

day_by_day.notes: Jewish Museum combo ticket: ~550 CZK (~€23). Closed on Saturdays. Classical concerts typically start at 19:30 or 20:00 — book ahead as September is peak season. Mucha Museum ~240 CZK (~€10).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or morning exploration to Vyšehrad — the lesser-known but equally impressive fortress with panoramic views of Prague, the ancient Romanesque Rotunda of St. Martin, and the famous cemetery where Dvořák and Smetana are buried. Peaceful and crowd-free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the trendy Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods on foot — browse vintage shops, visit the iconic Žižkov TV Tower (with baby sculptures by David Černý), and soak in the local café culture. This is where young Praguers actually live.
day_by_day.evening: Last evening in Prague — return to Old Town for a farewell dinner. Take a final nighttime walk across Charles Bridge and through the illuminated Old Town Square.

meals.breakfast: Café Jen (Vinohrady area) or similar local neighborhood café — granola, fresh juice, and good espresso
meals.lunch: Nase Maso (Our Meat) — legendary Old Town butcher-restaurant; try the steak sandwich or beef tartare; queue early as it fills fast
meals.dinner: V Zátiší — refined Czech-international cuisine; elegant but accessible mid-range pricing; perfect farewell Prague dinner

day_by_day.notes: Vyšehrad is free to enter (fortress grounds); panoramic views are spectacular in September light. Pack your bags tonight — early departure to Budapest tomorrow. Žižkov TV Tower observation deck: ~230 CZK (~€10).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Prague to Budapest by RegioJet or FlixBus train/bus (~6.5–7 hours) or Wizz Air/Czech Airlines flight (~1.5 hours). Recommended: morning train/bus departing ~08:00–09:00 for a scenic journey through Czech and Slovak countryside. Arrive Budapest early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into Budapest accommodation (recommend staying in District V — Belváros, or District VII — Jewish Quarter for best access). Orientation walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) with views of Buda Castle and Chain Bridge. Explore the elegant Váci Street area.
day_by_day.evening: First Budapest evening — cross the Chain Bridge to Buda side at sunset for golden-hour views of the Parliament building. Return to Pest for dinner in the lively Great Market Hall area or ruin bar district.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Prague hotel or grab pastries and coffee at Prague train station (Hlavní nádraží)
meals.lunch: On-board train snacks or stop at a platform café; alternatively eat after arrival in Budapest — try Bors GasztroBar (District VII) for legendary stuffed baguettes
meals.dinner: Első Pesti Rétesház — traditional Hungarian strudel house and restaurant; try gulyás (goulash), lángos, and fresh rétes (strudel) for dessert; very affordable

day_by_day.notes: RegioJet Prague–Budapest trains are comfortable with Wi-Fi and meal service — book in advance. If flying, allow time for airport transfers on both ends. September in Budapest is warm and beautiful — ideal travel weather.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill — take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) up from Clark Ádám Square. Visit the Royal Palace / Hungarian National Gallery, Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom), and the Fishermen's Bastion (Halászbástya) for the most iconic Budapest panorama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Óbuda and Margaret Island (Margit-sziget) — rent a bike or walk this car-free island in the Danube. Visit the musical fountain, Japanese garden, and medieval monastery ruins. Relaxed and very local Sunday vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's famous ruin bar scene — start at Szimpla Kert (the original ruin bar in District VII), the most iconic in the city. Explore the Jewish Quarter's eclectic nightlife and street art.

meals.breakfast: New York Café for a splurge-worthy breakfast in the world's most beautiful café (book ahead) — or affordable alternative: Madal Café for specialty coffee and pastries
meals.lunch: Margaret Island picnic — grab supplies from a local market or deli near the island; alternatively eat at the island's casual café
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food Court (District VII, outdoor) — multiple food trucks with Hungarian and international street food; lively Sunday atmosphere, very affordable

day_by_day.notes: Fishermen's Bastion is free to walk around (small fee for tower access). Matthias Church entry ~2,500 HUF (~€6.50). Funicular ~1,400 HUF (~€3.70) each way or walk up via Castle Hill path for free. Szimpla Kert also hosts a Sunday farmers market (10:00–14:00) — worth a visit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building (Országház) — one of the largest parliament buildings in the world and a masterpiece of Gothic Revival architecture. Guided tours run regularly and include the Crown Jewels of Hungary. Book tickets online in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and a deeply moving Holocaust memorial site. Afterward, browse the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) for Hungarian paprika, salami, Tokaji wine, and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Thermal bath experience — visit Széchenyi Baths (Széchenyi fürdő) in City Park for an authentic Budapest evening soak. The outdoor pools lit at night are magical. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

meals.breakfast: Local neighborhood bakery — try kürtőskalács (chimney cake) or a fresh kifli roll with butter and coffee from a street stall near your hotel
meals.lunch: Great Market Hall upper floor — traditional Hungarian lunch stalls serving lángos, stuffed cabbage, and goulash soup at very local prices
meals.dinner: Menza (District VI, Liszt Ferenc tér) — retro-chic Hungarian restaurant with modern takes on classics; excellent value, lively atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tour: ~8,000 HUF (~€21) for non-EU citizens; book 2–3 days ahead online. Great Synagogue: ~5,000 HUF (~€13). Széchenyi Baths: ~8,500–10,000 HUF (~€22–26) depending on locker/cabin choice. Bring flip-flops for the baths.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Museum of Fine Arts or the Palace of Art (Műcsarnok) — both flanking the grand square. Stroll through City Park (Városliget), see Vajdahunyad Castle, and visit the nearby Széchenyi thermal bath area in daylight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon exploration — walk the elegant Andrássy Avenue (a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard), stop at the Hungarian State Opera House for an exterior photo or a guided tour if available. Browse boutique shops and local design stores along the avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Budapest dinner in the Jewish Quarter or along the Danube embankment. End with a sunset or evening Danube river cruise for a spectacular final view of both cities' bridges and illuminated Parliament.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud (Vörösmarty Square) — Budapest's most historic café since 1858; indulge in a coffee and Esterházy torte or Gerbeaud slice for a classic farewell breakfast
meals.lunch: Borkonyha Winekitchen (District V) — Michelin Bib Gourmand Hungarian wine-focused restaurant; excellent value for a slightly elevated farewell lunch
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown or a riverside restaurant along the Danube Promenade — splurge slightly for the final night; alternatively, Hungarikum Bisztró for hearty traditional Hungarian classics at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Danube river cruise: evening illumination cruises run ~60–90 min from ~6,000–8,000 HUF (~€15–21); book at the dock or online. Andrássy Avenue Opera House tours: ~3,000–4,000 HUF. Pack bags tonight if departing early next day. Heroes' Square and City Park are free to explore.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Staré Město (Old Town), Prague Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury car service (e.g., Mercedes E-Class or similar) to your boutique hotel in Staré Město (Old Town). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the heart of Staré Město. Stroll across the iconic Charles Bridge, admire the 30 Baroque statues, and soak in panoramic views of the Vltava River. Continue to the Old Town Square to see the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the Gothic Týn Church facade. Keep the pace relaxed after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric lanes of Josefov (the Jewish Quarter) at golden hour. Enjoy a pre-dinner aperitif at a rooftop bar — try the terrace at Café Savoy or the rooftop at Hotel Paris Prague — before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light welcome bite at the hotel or a quick stop at Café Louvre for Czech open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky) and coffee upon arrival
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — Prague's Michelin-starred gem offering a tasting menu rooted in historic Czech recipes, paired with curated Czech wines. Reserve the chef's table for an intimate experience.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private airport transfer before arrival. Confirm dinner reservation at La Degustation well in advance — it books out weeks ahead. Weather in Prague in mid-September is typically mild (15–20°C), ideal for walking; pack a light jacket for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex (Pražský hrad) exploration. Arrive early (by 9:00) to beat crowds. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral, the Royal Palace, the Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička), and the Basilica of St. George. Hire a private licensed guide for a 2-hour deep-dive into Bohemian royal history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood. Visit the Baroque St. Nicholas Church and explore the hidden Wallenstein Garden. Cross back via Charles Bridge for a leisurely afternoon. Stop at a premium gallery — DOX Centre for Contemporary Arts or the Museum of Decorative Arts — for cultural enrichment.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical concert at the Rudolfinum (home of the Czech Philharmonic) or a chamber music performance inside the stunning Lobkowicz Palace. Prague's September concert season is in full swing.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your boutique property — request a full Czech spread with local cheeses, cold cuts, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Terasa U Zlaté Studně (Terrace at the Golden Well Hotel) — stunning hilltop terrace in Malá Strana with refined Czech-European cuisine and castle views
meals.dinner: Field Restaurant — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant in Staré Město with seasonal tasting menus and an exceptional natural wine list

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle complex in the world — wear comfortable walking shoes. The private guide can be arranged through your hotel concierge. Book Rudolfinum tickets online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) with a private guide. Tour the six historic synagogues (Old-New Synagogue, Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting Holocaust memorial, Spanish Synagogue) and the Old Jewish Cemetery — one of the most atmospheric sites in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — Prague's elegant residential districts with Art Nouveau architecture, independent boutiques, and the iconic Žižkov Television Tower (with David Černý's crawling babies). Visit the National Museum on Wenceslas Square, freshly restored to its Neo-Renaissance grandeur.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium Czech food and wine tasting experience. Book a private tasting session at Vinograf wine bar featuring Moravian wines paired with artisan Czech charcuterie and cheeses, followed by a nighttime walk along the illuminated Vltava embankment.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café Imperial — a grand Art Nouveau brasserie with original ceramic mosaic interiors; order the svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) for a classic Czech experience
meals.dinner: Eska — an award-winning modern Czech restaurant in Karlín district focusing on fermentation, open-fire cooking, and locally sourced ingredients. Pair with their natural wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: The Pinkas Synagogue is deeply moving — allow quiet time. Josefov entry requires a combined ticket; purchase online to skip queues. Eska is a short taxi ride from Old Town — worth every minute.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Prague — optional visit to the Mucha Museum (dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha) or a private cooking class focusing on traditional Bohemian cuisine (dumplings, svíčková, trdelník). Alternatively, browse the antique markets at Náměstí Míru.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Prague to Budapest by premium car service or first-class rail (Railjet — approximately 7 hours, scenic and comfortable) or a short 1-hour flight. Check into your luxury hotel in Budapest upon arrival. (Recommend: Four Seasons Gresham Palace or Aria Hotel Budapest.)
day_by_day.evening: First impressions of Budapest — a gentle evening walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó), admiring the illuminated Parliament Building and Chain Bridge. Enjoy a welcome cocktail at the rooftop bar of your hotel with panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast in Prague — final Czech morning spread
meals.lunch: Pre-transfer lunch at Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved Prague beer hall serving fresh Pilsner Urquell tank beer and elevated Czech pub classics in a lively but quality setting
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown Budapest — Hungary's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering an innovative Hungarian-European tasting menu. Perfect first-night Budapest dining.

day_by_day.notes: If traveling by train, book first-class Railjet seats well in advance — the Prague–Budapest route is scenic through the Bohemian and Moravian countryside. Flying is faster but the train experience is quintessentially Central European. Confirm Budapest hotel check-in time.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Buda Castle Hill. Take the historic funicular (Budavári Sikló) up to the Royal Palace complex. Visit the Hungarian National Gallery inside the palace for world-class Hungarian fine art. Walk through the medieval Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) for the most iconic views over the Danube and Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) — a stunning Gothic-Baroque masterpiece. Descend to explore the Cave Church (Sziklatemplom) carved into the cliff. Cross the Chain Bridge on foot to the Pest side and explore the elegant Andrássy Avenue (a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard) lined with Neo-Renaissance palaces, boutiques, and embassies.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House — one of the most beautiful opera houses in Europe. Pre-book premium seats for a ballet or opera production. The September season opening is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — if at Gresham Palace, the breakfast spread overlooking the Chain Bridge is unmissable
meals.lunch: Halászbástya Restaurant — right at the Fisherman's Bastion with panoramic Danube views; order traditional Hungarian fish soup (halászlé) and roasted duck
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Borkonyha Winekitchen — a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant near the Opera House, celebrated for its Hungarian wine pairings and modern Magyar cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book Opera House tickets months in advance for September — opening season performances sell out quickly. The Fisherman's Bastion is free to explore (upper terraces have a small fee). Andrássy Avenue is perfect for a leisurely afternoon stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in a premium Budapest thermal spa experience. Visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath (the largest in Europe, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque palace in City Park) or the more intimate and architecturally breathtaking Gellért Baths. Book a private VIP cabin and massage treatment for a truly luxurious morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Great Market Hall (Központi Vásárcsarnok) — Budapest's magnificent iron-and-glass 19th-century market. Browse artisan stalls for Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wines, foie gras, Herend porcelain, and embroidered folk textiles as premium souvenirs. Then visit the Dohány Street Synagogue — the largest in Europe and a deeply significant cultural landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset river cruise on the Danube aboard a premium private boat. Watch the Parliament, bridges, and castle light up as dusk falls — one of the most spectacular urban panoramas in the world. Champagne service included.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most historic and opulent café (est. 1858). Order the Esterházy torte, Dobos torte, and a Hungarian coffee ritual
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant — a two-Michelin-starred restaurant in the heart of Budapest offering a theatrical Hungarian haute cuisine tasting experience with exceptional service and wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book the Gellért or Széchenyi spa VIP experience through your hotel concierge to guarantee private cabin access. The private Danube cruise should be arranged 48 hours in advance — sunset timing shifts daily in September (around 19:00). Onyx requires formal attire.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to the Danube Bend (Dunakanyar) — one of Central Europe's most scenic river landscapes. Private driver takes you to the medieval town of Visegrád (hilltop citadel with panoramic views), then to the Baroque masterpiece town of Esztergom (Hungary's religious capital, home to the massive Esztergom Basilica — the largest church in Hungary).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the charming artist town of Szentendre — a colorful Serbian-Hungarian village filled with galleries, artisan workshops, ceramic studios, and excellent wine bars. Browse the open-air village museum (Skanzen) and pick up unique handcrafted souvenirs. Return to Budapest by private car.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final full evening in Budapest. Explore the ruin bars of the Jewish Quarter — Szimpla Kert is the most famous — for a culturally unique Budapest experience. These eclectic, multi-room bars set in crumbling courtyards are a Budapest original. End the night with a nightcap at a sophisticated cocktail bar.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch in Szentendre — assembled from local deli shops and bakeries in the town square, or sit-down at Rab Ráby restaurant for traditional Hungarian cuisine with a riverside terrace
meals.dinner: Stand25 Bisztró — a beloved Budapest bistro known for its modern Hungarian comfort food, excellent natural wines, and warm neighborhood atmosphere. A perfect relaxed final evening meal.

day_by_day.notes: The Danube Bend excursion covers approximately 100km round trip — a private driver is strongly recommended over public transport for comfort and flexibility. Allow 7–8 hours for the full loop. Szimpla Kert is busiest after 21:00 on weekdays — arrive early for a quieter experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last-minute exploration of the elegant Lipótváros (Leopold Town) district around the Parliament Building. Walk along the Danube bank to see the powerful 'Shoes on the Danube Bank' Holocaust memorial — a deeply moving and important historical site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti Múzeum) in Heroes' Square — housing one of Central Europe's finest collections of European masters (El Greco, Raphael, Goya). Alternatively, browse the luxury boutiques along Váci Street or the high-end designer stores on Andrássy Avenue for final souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations. Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport. Final farewell to Eastern Europe.

meals.breakfast: Grand final in-hotel breakfast — take your time and savor the last morning
meals.lunch: Páva Restaurant at the Corinthia Hotel — an elegant all-day dining brasserie perfect for a refined final Budapest lunch with Hungarian classics elevated to fine dining standards
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner at New York Café (the 'most beautiful café in the world') — a gilded Neo-Baroque palace café serving Hungarian and international dishes in an unforgettable setting

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for the airport transfer and check-in. Budapest airport is approximately 30–45 minutes from the city center. New York Café requires reservations even for coffee — book ahead. Consider purchasing Tokaji Aszú dessert wine and Hungarian paprika as premium take-home gifts from the Great Market Hall (best done on Day 6).
